title: Basic STOMPI Word Order
subtitle: Master the golden rule of Afrikaans sentence structure
keyPoint: Standard Afrikaans sentences strictly follow the STOMPI sequence: Subject, Verb 1, Time, Object, Manner, Place, and Verb 2.

useCases.label: Simple S-V1-O Sentence
useCases.example: Ek eet 'n appel.

useCases.label: Full Time-Object-Place Sequence
useCases.example: Ons drink nou koffie in die kombuis.

useCases.label: Auxiliary with Final Verb (V2)
useCases.example: Hulle sal môre die kar vinnig was.

examples.en: Ek lees elke dag 'n boek.
Hulle ry vandag per trein na die stad.
examples.highlight: vandag per trein na die stad

examples.en: Pa drink nou rustig koffie op die stoep.
examples.highlight: nou rustig koffie op die stoep

examples.en: Ons gaan vanaand lekker kos by die restaurant eet.
examples.highlight: gaan vanaand lekker kos by die restaurant eet

examples.en: Sy sal môre die pakkie vinnig pos toe neem.
examples.highlight: sal môre die pakkie vinnig pos toe neem

mistakes.wrong: Ek eet by die huis nou 'n appel.
mistakes.right: Ek eet nou 'n appel by die huis.
mistakes.note: Time must precede Object, and Object must precede Place (T-O-M-P).

mistakes.wrong: Sy sal lees 'n boek môre.
mistakes.note: Verb 2 belongs at the very end of the clause in compound verb structures.

mistakes.wrong: Gister ek het geslaap.
mistakes.note: When starting with Time, Verb 1 must stay in second position, causing subject-verb inversion.

quiz.question: Choose the correct STOMPI order: 'We are drinking coffee in the garden now.'
options: Ons drink in die tuin nou koffie.
Ons drink nou koffie in die tuin.
Ons nou drink koffie in die tuin.
Ons koffie drink nou in die tuin.
quiz.explanation: Time (nou) must come before Object (koffie), which comes before Place (in die tuin).

quiz.question: Where does the main verb go in: 'Hulle wil môre 'n fliek ___.'
quiz.explanation: In sentences with modal or auxiliary verbs (V1 = wil), the infinitive main verb (V2 = kyk) is placed at the very end.

quiz.question: Identify the correct order: 'Môre ___ ons die eksamen skryf.'
quiz.explanation: Verb 1 (sal) must occupy the second position immediately after the fronted Time phrase (Môre).

quiz.question: Which sentence follows strict STOMPI order?
options: Hy ry met die bus skool toe elke oggend.
Hy ry elke oggend met die bus skool toe.
Hy elke oggend ry met die bus skool toe.
Hy ry skool toe elke oggend met die bus.
quiz.explanation: Time (elke oggend) precedes Manner (met die bus), which precedes Place (skool toe).

tip: Remember: STOMPI never fails for statements! If you move Time to the front for emphasis, Verb 1 remains in position 2, immediately followed by the Subject.

title: The Double Negative (Nie ... Nie)
subtitle: Mastering the obligatory sentence-final negation marker
keyPoint: In Afrikaans, negative statements require a second 'nie' at the end of the sentence or clause, framing the negated information.

cells: Hy eet nie die vleis nie.

useCases.label: Basic Clause Negation
useCases.example: Ek verstaan dit nie.

useCases.label: Full Negation Frame
useCases.example: Sy gaan nie vandag skool toe nie.

useCases.label: Negative Pronoun/Adverb
useCases.example: Daar is niks in die boks nie.

examples.en: Ek praat nie Engels nie.
Ons wil nie nou huis toe gaan nie.
examples.highlight: nie nou huis toe gaan nie

examples.en: Sy sien nooit die son nie.
Hulle het nie gister gekom nie.
Niemand ken die antwoord nie.

mistakes.wrong: Ek hou nie van tee.
mistakes.right: Ek hou nie van tee nie.
mistakes.note: Never omit the mandatory second 'nie' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Hy eet nie niks nie.
mistakes.note: Words like 'niks', 'niemand', and 'nooit' already act as the first negative; do not add the first 'nie'.

mistakes.wrong: Ek weet nie nie.
mistakes.note: When the verb immediately precedes the end of the clause with no other words, only one 'nie' is used.

quiz.question: Complete the negative sentence: 'Hulle bly nie in Kaapstad ___.'
quiz.explanation: Standard Afrikaans clauses require a closing 'nie' at the very end.

quiz.question: How do you say 'Nobody is coming'?
quiz.explanation: 'Niemand' functions as the first negative, so you only need the final 'nie' at the end.

quiz.question: Which sentence has correct double negation?
options: Ek wil nie nou slaap nie.
quiz.explanation: The first 'nie' comes right after Verb 1 and the second 'nie' closes the sentence.

quiz.question: Translate the concept: 'She does not eat meat.'
options: Beide A en B is korrek.
quiz.explanation: Both 'nie ... nie' and 'geen ... nie' are grammatically valid ways to negate this sentence.

tip: Think of Afrikaans negation like quotation marks or parentheses: the first marker (nie, nooit, niemand) opens the negative thought, and the final 'nie' closes it.

title: Base Verbs and Lack of Person Conjugation
subtitle: No verb endings: one single form for all pronouns
keyPoint: Afrikaans verbs never change for person or number (I, you, he, we, they all use the exact same form).

useCases.label: Regular Action Verb
useCases.example: Hy werk elke dag hard.

useCases.label: Irregular 'to be' (wees -> is)
useCases.example: Hulle is baie gelukkig.

useCases.label: Irregular 'to have' (hê -> het)
useCases.example: Ons het twee honde.

examples.en: Ek drink water en sy drink melk.
Die kinders speel buite in die tuin.
Vandag is die weer baie mooi.
Hy het 'n nuwe fiets.
Ons verstaan die les baie goed.

mistakes.wrong: Hy werks by die bank.
mistakes.note: Do not add an English-style '-s' for third person singular; Afrikaans verbs never inflect.

mistakes.wrong: Ons bint bly om jou te sien.
mistakes.right: Ons is bly om jou te sien.
mistakes.note: The present tense of 'wees' (to be) is always 'is', regardless of subject.

mistakes.wrong: Ek he 'n vraag.
mistakes.note: The present indicative form of the verb 'hê' is always 'het'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Sy ___ elke oggend koffie.'
quiz.explanation: Afrikaans verbs keep the bare base form with no person suffixes.

quiz.question: Select the correct form: 'Ons ___ moeg na die lang dag.'
quiz.explanation: 'is' is the invariable present tense of the verb 'wees' for all persons.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Julle ___ baie boeke.'
quiz.explanation: The present tense form of 'to have' is 'het' for all subjects.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly expresses 'The dogs run'?
quiz.explanation: Plural subjects take the identical base verb form without endings.

tip: Afrikaans has zero conjugation tables! Learn the base stem of a verb once, and you can immediately use it with every single pronoun.

title: Past Tense with 'Het' and 'Ge-'
subtitle: How Afrikaans expresses all past events with one simple structure
keyPoint: Afrikaans has only one general past tense, formed by putting auxiliary 'het' in Verb 1 position and the main verb with prefix 'ge-' at the end.

cells: Verbs with be-, ge-, her-, ont-, ver- do NOT take ge-

useCases.label: Regular Past Action
useCases.example: Ek het gister 'n boek gelees.

useCases.label: Past Tense of 'to be' (was)
useCases.example: Hy was verlede week siek.

useCases.label: Verb with Inseparable Prefix
useCases.example: Ons het die les dadelik verstaan.

examples.en: Sy het vanoggend vroeg opgestaan.
Ons het gister lekker gekook.
Hulle het die hele koek geëet.
Ek het my sleutels verloor.
Hy het verlede jaar 'n huis gekoop.

mistakes.wrong: Ek het gister geet 'n appel.
mistakes.note: The ge- past participle must go to the Verb 2 position at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ons het die probleem geverstaan.
mistakes.note: Verbs starting with inseparable prefixes like 'ver-', 'be-', or 'ont-' never take an extra 'ge-'.

mistakes.wrong: Hy het gewees siek.
mistakes.note: The verb 'wees' (to be) uses its simple past form 'was' rather than 'het gewees' in standard everyday speech.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Hulle het gister sokker ___.'
quiz.explanation: Regular verbs form their past participle with 'ge-' + base stem (gespeel) at the end.

quiz.question: How do you form the past of 'verkoop' (to sell)?
quiz.explanation: Verbs beginning with prefixes like 'ver-' do not add 'ge-'; the form remains 'verkoop'.

quiz.question: Where does 'het' go in: 'Gister ___ ek 'n brief geskryf.'
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary 'het' must take the Verb 1 position, which is position 2 following 'Gister'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I made food'?
quiz.explanation: Auxiliary 'het' takes position 2 and participle 'gemaak' stands at the very end.

tip: Good news: Afrikaans has no separate past continuous or past perfect in everyday speech. 'Ek het geëet' translates 'I ate', 'I have eaten', and 'I was eating'!

title: Modal Auxiliaries and Verb Placement
subtitle: Expressing ability, necessity, and desire using kan, moet, and wil
keyPoint: Modal auxiliaries take the Verb 1 slot in the sentence, sending the bare infinitive of the main action verb to the Verb 2 slot at the end.

cells: Ons moet nou huis toe gaan.

useCases.label: Ability (kan)
useCases.example: Sy kan vlot Afrikaans praat.

useCases.label: Obligation (moet)
useCases.example: Jy moet jou groente eet.

useCases.label: Intention or Future (wil / sal)
useCases.example: Ons sal môre die werk klaarmaak.

examples.en: Ek wil 'n koppie koffie drink.
Jy moet jou kamer vandag skoonmaak.
Hulle kan baie goed swem.
Ons sal môre vroeg vertrek.
Mag ek asseblief die venster oopmaak?
examples.highlight: Mag ek asseblief die venster oopmaak

mistakes.wrong: Ek wil om koffie te drink.
mistakes.note: Modal verbs in Afrikaans take a bare infinitive; do not add 'om ... te'.

mistakes.wrong: Hy kan praat baie goed Afrikaans.
mistakes.right: Hy kan baie goed Afrikaans praat.
mistakes.note: The main infinitive verb must be sent to the very end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ons moets nou gaan.
mistakes.note: Modal verbs never inflect for person or number.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Jy ___ nou jou huiswerk doen.'
quiz.explanation: The invariable present form for 'must/should' is 'moet'.

quiz.question: Where does the main verb belong: 'Hulle wil vandag 'n motor ___.'
quiz.explanation: The bare infinitive (koop) belongs at the end of the clause in Verb 2 position.

quiz.question: Which modal expresses permission ('may')?
quiz.explanation: 'mag' expresses permission (equivalent to 'may' or 'allowed to').

quiz.question: Select the correct sentence:
quiz.explanation: The modal 'kan' sits in Verb 1 position, while the main action verb 'speel' sits at the end in Verb 2 position.

tip: Unlike English, Afrikaans modals never take 'to' (om te). Just pair the modal in Verb 1 with the bare main verb kicked to the very end of the clause.

title: Noun Plurals and Diminutives
subtitle: Adding -e, -s, and diminutive suffixes like -tjie
keyPoint: Afrikaans nouns form plurals mainly with -e or -s, while diminutives add endings like -tjie or -ie with predictable vowel and consonant adjustments.

cells: Add -e; double vowel drops one letter if syllable opens
Add -s on words ending in unaccented syllables or -el/-en/-er
Add -tjie after vowels, l, n, or r preceded by long vowel/diphthong
dog -> little dog / chair -> little chair

useCases.label: Everyday Plurals
useCases.example: Die honde blaf in die straat.

useCases.label: Small Objects (-tjie / -ie)
useCases.example: Ek drink 'n koppie koffie by die tafeltjie.

useCases.label: Endearment and Suffix Shifts
useCases.example: Die klein katjie slaap op die kussing.

examples.en: Die bome in ons tuin is baie oud.
Sy koop drie nuwe tafels vir die kantoor.
Daar sit 'n klein voëltjie op die heining.
Ons plant 'n nuwe boompie voor die venster.
Die kinders speel met hulle speelgoed buite.

mistakes.wrong: twee boome
mistakes.note: When adding -e creates an open syllable, twin vowels (aa, ee, oo, uu) reduce to a single vowel letter.

mistakes.wrong: een klein tafeltje
mistakes.note: Afrikaans diminutive endings use -ie (such as -tjie or -jie), never the Dutch spelling -tje.

mistakes.wrong: hondejie
mistakes.note: Words ending in -d or -t simply take -jie (forming -tjie or -djie pronounced identically as /ki/).

quiz.question: Select the correct plural form of 'man' (man): 'Daar is vyf ___ in die vertrek.'
quiz.explanation: Short vowel words ending in a single consonant double the consonant when taking -e: man -> manne.

quiz.question: What is the correct diminutive for 'arm' (arm)?
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in -rm or -lm take -pie in the diminutive: arm -> armpie.

quiz.question: Choose the correct plural: 'Die onderwyser lees drie ___.'
quiz.explanation: Most monosyllabic nouns ending in a consonant take -e in the plural: boek -> boeke.

quiz.question: What is the diminutive of 'kat' (cat)?
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in -t take -jie to form -tjie: kat -> katjie.

tip: Remember: twin vowels drop a letter in open syllables (boom -> bome), while single short vowels double the consonant (pen -> penne).

title: Attributive Adjective Inflection
subtitle: Adding -e to adjectives placed directly before nouns
keyPoint: Attributive adjectives before nouns often take an inflected -e ending depending on syllable count, ending consonants, and vowel length.

cells: Adjectives ending in -r preceded by long vowels/diphthongs

useCases.label: Describing Objects Directly
useCases.example: Hy lees 'n interessante boek oor geskiedenis.

useCases.label: Phonetic Dropping (-d to -e)
useCases.example: Ons stap deur die koue wind.

useCases.label: Predicate (Uninflected) vs Attributive
useCases.example: Die man is oud, maar hy dra 'n ou jas.

examples.en: Ons bly in 'n pragtige huis naby die see.
Hy drink graag koue melk in die oggend.
Sy koop 'n vinnige motor vir werk toe gaan.
Dit is 'n hoë boom met baie blare.
Sy het 'n nuwe rok vir die partytjie gekoop.

mistakes.wrong: Die boek is interessante.
mistakes.note: Predicate adjectives (placed after 'is/was' with no noun following) never take the inflected -e.

mistakes.wrong: 'n koude nag
mistakes.note: Adjectives ending in -d after a diphthong drop the 'd' completely when taking -e (koud -> koue).

mistakes.wrong: 'n rooie appel
mistakes.note: Basic monosyllabic colours like rooi, blou, wit, and swart generally remain uninflected before nouns.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Sy woon in 'n ___ dorpie.' (mooi)
quiz.explanation: Monosyllabic adjectives ending in a diphthong like 'mooi' or 'vry' typically do not take -e.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Hulle drink ___ sap.' (vars)
quiz.explanation: Monosyllabic adjectives ending in -rs like vars or naar do not take an inflected -e.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Dit was 'n ___ ervaring.' (ongelooflik)
quiz.explanation: Polysyllabic adjectives take -e when used attributively before a noun: ongelooflike.

quiz.question: Choose the inflected form of 'oud' (old): 'Hy dra 'n ___ hoed.'
quiz.explanation: 'Oud' has the irregular attributive form 'ou' before a singular or general noun ('n ou hoed).

tip: Adjectives after the verb (predicative) stay bare: 'Die motor is vinnig.' Adjectives right before the noun (attributive) often inflect: ''n Vinnige motor.'

title: Separable vs. Inseparable Verbs
subtitle: Distinguishing aanbreek from onthou in past tense
keyPoint: Separable prefix verbs insert 'ge-' between the prefix and base verb in the past tense, whereas inseparable prefix verbs never take 'ge-'.

cells: Unstressed (be-, ge-, her-, er-, ont-, ver-)
Prefix splits to end of clause in simple present
Prefix stays attached to the verb stem

useCases.label: Separable in Present Tense
useCases.example: Hy maak elke oggend die venster oop.

useCases.label: Separable in Perfect Tense
useCases.example: Ons het die aansoekvorm gister ingevul.

useCases.label: Inseparable (Zero 'ge-')
useCases.example: Ek het dadelik my ou onderwyser herken.

examples.en: Hy bel sy vriend vanaand op.
Die vergadering het reeds begin.
Hulle het al die ligte afgeskakel.
Ek het jou boodskap gister ontvang.
Sy maak die deur vir die gaste oop.

mistakes.wrong: Ek het hom geverstaan.
mistakes.note: Inseparable prefixes (be-, her-, ont-, ver-) never take 'ge-' in the past tense.

mistakes.wrong: Hy het geaanhou met praat.
mistakes.note: Separable verbs insert -ge- between the prefix and the stem: aan + ge + hou.

mistakes.wrong: Hy opmaak die boks.
mistakes.note: In the simple present, separable prefixes split and move to the end of the clause.

quiz.question: Choose the correct past tense form: 'Ons het gister die nuwe reëls ___.' (aanvaar - inseparable)
quiz.explanation: 'Aanvaar' is inseparable (accent on -vaar), so it takes no 'ge-' prefix in the past tense: 'het aanvaar'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct past tense form: 'Sy het haar ouers ___.' (opbel - separable)
quiz.explanation: 'Opbel' is separable; the past marker -ge- is inserted between the prefix and stem: op + ge + bel.

quiz.question: How do you say in the present: 'He invites his friends' (nooi ... uit)?
quiz.explanation: In simple present clauses, the separable prefix ('uit') shifts to the end of the clause.

quiz.question: Complete the past tense: 'Ek het my sleutels ___.' (verloor - inseparable)
quiz.explanation: Verbs beginning with 'ver-' are inseparable and never receive 'ge-': 'het verloor'.

tip: Mnemonic for inseparable prefixes with zero 'ge-': Be-Her-Er-Ont-Ver-Ge (B-HERO-VG). If it begins with one of these unstressed prefixes, never add 'ge-'!

title: Conjunction Groups & Word Order
subtitle: Navigating Group 1, 2, and 3 conjunctions
keyPoint: Afrikaans conjunctions dictate word order: Group 1 leaves normal SVO order, Group 2 triggers verb inversion, and Group 3 pushes the verb to the end.

cells: Verb moves to the clause end

useCases.label: Group 1: Group-neutral Linking
useCases.example: Hy wil saamkom, maar hy het nie geld nie.

useCases.label: Group 2: Causality with Inversion
useCases.example: Dit reën hard, daarom bly ons by die huis.

useCases.label: Group 3: Dependent Subordinate Clauses
useCases.example: Ek weet dat sy elke dag hard leer.

examples.en: Hy gaan winkel toe, want hy het brood nodig.
Ek het my beursie vergeet, daarom kan ek nie betaal nie.
Ons bly binne omdat die weer so sleg is.
examples.highlight: omdat die weer so sleg is

examples.en: Toe die son opkom, het die voëls begin sing.
Jy moet nou eet, anders word die kos koud.

mistakes.wrong: Hy bly by die huis want hy is siek.
mistakes.right: Hy bly by die huis, want hy is siek.
mistakes.note: In Group 1, 'want' keeps normal order (SVO: hy is), but learners often confuse it with 'omdat' (which sends 'is' to the end).

mistakes.wrong: Dit reën, daarom ons bly by die huis.
mistakes.right: Dit reën, daarom bly ons by die huis.
mistakes.note: Group 2 conjunctions (like daarom) require immediate inversion of the verb and subject: daarom + bly + ons.

mistakes.wrong: Ek weet dat hy kom môre.
mistakes.right: Ek weet dat hy môre kom.
mistakes.note: Group 3 conjunctions (like dat, omdat) push the finite verb to the very end of the sub-clause.

quiz.question: Complete the Group 2 sentence: 'Ek is moeg, daarom ___ ek vroeg slaap.'
quiz.explanation: Group 2 words like 'daarom' cause inversion: Conjunction + Verb + Subject ('daarom gaan ek...').

quiz.question: Complete the Group 3 sentence: 'Sy sê dat sy vanaand 'n fliek ___.'
quiz.explanation: Group 3 conjunction 'dat' forces verbs to the end of the clause ('sal kyk').

quiz.question: Which conjunction belongs to Group 1 (normal SVO order)?
quiz.explanation: 'Want' is a Group 1 conjunction; the word order following it remains Subject + Verb.

quiz.question: Complete the conditional clause: 'As dit reën, ___ ons nie park toe nie.'
quiz.explanation: When a subordinate clause (Group 3 with 'As') comes first, the main clause begins with the inverted verb: 'gaan ons'.

tip: Compare 'want' vs 'omdat': '...want hy IS siek' (Group 1: verb stays second) vs '...omdat hy siek IS' (Group 3: verb goes to end).

title: Future Tense with 'Sal'
subtitle: Forming future statements using Verb 1 and Verb 2 brackets
keyPoint: To form the future tense, place the auxiliary 'sal' in the Verb 1 slot and push the bare infinitive verb to the end of the clause in Verb 2.

cells: Bare main verb at end of clause

useCases.label: Expressing Future Intent
useCases.example: Ek sal jou môreoggend by die kantoor sien.

useCases.label: Future with Negation (Double Nie)
useCases.example: Hulle sal nie die wedstryd wen nie.

useCases.label: Polite Offers / Promises
useCases.example: Ons sal die kos vir die gaste voorberei.

examples.en: Ons sal volgende week Kaapstad toe ry.
Ek sal jou vanaand na ete opbel.
Die trein sal binne tien minute hier aankom.
Sy sal nie die eksamen sonder voorbereiding slaag nie.
Wat sal jy met daardie geld maak?

mistakes.wrong: Ek sal gaan koop brood.
mistakes.note: The main verb(s) must go to the very end of the clause (Verb 2 position).

mistakes.wrong: Ons sal gekoop 'n huis.
mistakes.note: 'Sal' takes the plain infinitive without 'ge-'; 'gekoop' is past tense.

mistakes.wrong: Hy sal kom nie.
mistakes.note: Negative sentences with 'sal' require 'nie' after the auxiliary/object and a final 'nie' at the clause end.

quiz.question: Complete the future tense: 'Hulle ___ môre 'n nuwe huis besoek.'
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary verb for future tense in Afrikaans is 'sal'.

quiz.question: Where does the main verb go in: 'Ons sal môre die rekening ___' (betaal)?
quiz.explanation: The main verb appears in its base infinitive form at the end of the sentence: 'betaal'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence order for future tense:
quiz.explanation: STOMPI word order dictates: Subject (Ek) + V1 (sal) + Time (môre) + Object ('n boek) + V2 (koop).

quiz.question: Complete the negative future sentence: 'Hy sal dit nie ___ nie.'
quiz.explanation: In future negative sentences, the base infinitive is placed before the final 'nie': '...nie verstaan nie.'

tip: Think of 'sal' and the end verb as bookends: 'sal' opens the action in slot 2, and the infinitive closes the clause right at the end.

title: Personal Object Marker 'Vir'
subtitle: Marking human direct objects to avoid ambiguity and sound natural
keyPoint: In Afrikaans, the preposition 'vir' is frequently placed before animate direct objects, especially personal pronouns and proper names, to clearly designate the receiver of an action.

useCases.label: Personal Pronouns
useCases.example: Ons ken vir haar baie goed.

useCases.label: Proper Names
useCases.example: Hulle soek al die hele oggend vir Pieter.

useCases.label: Disambiguation
useCases.example: Die leeu byt vir die jagter.

examples.en: Ek sien vir jou by die skool.
Het jy gister vir Sarie gebel?
Die hond jaag vir hom in die tuin rond.
Ons wag al lank vir ma.
Die polisie soek vir die dief.

mistakes.wrong: Ek lees vir die koerant elke oggend.
mistakes.right: Ek lees die koerant elke oggend.
mistakes.note: Do not insert 'vir' before inanimate objects like books or newspapers.

mistakes.wrong: Sy sien vir dit op die tafel.
mistakes.right: Sy sien dit op die tafel.
mistakes.note: Inanimate 'dit' should never take the personal object marker 'vir'.

mistakes.wrong: Hy skop vir die bal oor die heining.
mistakes.right: Hy skop die bal oor die heining.
mistakes.note: 'Bal' is an inanimate object, so direct 'vir' cannot be used.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'I am helping Anna today' -> 'Ek help vandag ___.'
quiz.explanation: In Afrikaans, animate direct objects such as names are preceded by 'vir'.

quiz.question: Choose the sentence that incorrectly uses 'vir':
quiz.explanation: 'Sleutels' (keys) is an inanimate noun and cannot take direct personal 'vir'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'We saw him yesterday'?
options: Ons het gister aan hom gesien.
Ons het gister vir hom gesien.
Ons het gister van hom gesien.
quiz.explanation: Personal pronouns acting as direct objects typically take 'vir' ('vir hom').

quiz.question: Which object can correctly take the personal marker 'vir'?
quiz.explanation: 'Die dokter' is animate and human, making 'vir die dokter' natural as a direct object.

tip: Think of 'vir' before a person as an accusative flag: use it when referring to people or beloved pets, but never for inanimate things!

title: Pronominal Adverbs (Daar- and Waar- Compounds)
subtitle: Combining adverbs with prepositions instead of using preposition + 'dit'
keyPoint: In Afrikaans, you cannot combine a preposition directly with the inanimate pronoun 'dit'; instead, replace 'dit' with 'daar-' (or 'waar-' in questions) fused to the preposition.

useCases.label: Statement with Daar-
useCases.example: Die boks is leeg, daar is niks daarin nie.

useCases.label: Question with Waar-
useCases.example: Waarmee sny jy die brood?

useCases.label: Separated Compounds
useCases.example: Daar dink ek glad nie aan nie.

examples.en: Wat wil jy daarmee doen?
Ons praat gereeld daaroor.
Waarna kyk julle nou?
Ek betaal met graagte daarvoor.
Daar steek geen waarheid daarin nie.

mistakes.wrong: Ek stem nie saam met dit nie.
mistakes.right: Ek stem nie daarmee saam nie.
mistakes.note: 'Met dit' is a direct English calque; use 'daarmee' ('met' mutates to '-mee').

mistakes.wrong: Wat dink jy van dit?
mistakes.note: Use 'daarvan' rather than 'van dit' when referring to inanimate ideas or things.

mistakes.wrong: Hy kyk vir dit.
mistakes.note: Preposition 'na' combines with 'daar-' to become 'daarna' when pointing to things.

quiz.question: How do you ask 'What are you waiting for?' in Afrikaans?
quiz.explanation: In questions, 'vir' + 'wat' merges into the pronominal adverb 'waarvoor'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct replacement for '*met dit':
quiz.explanation: When combined with 'daar-' or 'waar-', the preposition 'met' irregularily changes into '-mee'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Die glas val en al die water loop ___ uit.'
quiz.explanation: 'Uit' (out of) combines with 'daar-' to form 'daaruit' (out of it).

quiz.question: Which form is grammatically incorrect in standard Afrikaans?
quiz.explanation: 'Oor dit' is an ungrammatical calque from English; standard Afrikaans requires 'daaroor'.

tip: Remember special mutating prepositions: 'met' becomes '-mee' (daarmee), and 'tot' becomes '-toe' (daartoe)!

title: Passive Voice with 'Word' and 'Is'
subtitle: Mastering present passive ('word') and past passive ('is')
keyPoint: Afrikaans uses the auxiliary 'word' for the present passive and 'is' (not 'het') for the past passive, introducing the agent with 'deur'.

useCases.label: Present Action
useCases.example: Die motors word daagliks gewas.

useCases.label: Past Event
useCases.example: Die huis is verlede jaar gebou.

useCases.label: Known Agent with Deur
useCases.example: Die toespraak word deur die president gelewer.

examples.en: Die kos word deur my ouma gekook.
Al die kaartjies is gister verkoop.
Die venster word nou skoongemaak.
Die hond is deur 'n veearts behandel.
Nuwe reëls word vandag aangekondig.

mistakes.wrong: Die boek het geskryf deur haar.
mistakes.right: Die boek is deur haar geskryf.
mistakes.note: Never use 'het' for past passive; Afrikaans uses 'is + ge-participle'.

mistakes.wrong: Die werk word doen van my.
mistakes.right: Die werk word deur my gedoen.
mistakes.note: The agent preposition in passive clauses is 'deur', not 'van'.

mistakes.wrong: Die lied is geword gesing.
mistakes.note: Past passive does not retain 'word'; 'word' is entirely replaced by 'is'.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The car is being washed right now'?
quiz.explanation: The present passive uses 'word + ge-participle' ('word ... gewas').

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly expresses the past passive: 'The bread was baked by mother'?
options: Die brood het deur ma gebak.
Die brood was gebak deur ma.
Die brood is deur ma gebak.
Die brood word deur ma gebak het.
quiz.explanation: Past passive is formed using 'is' and places the ge-participle clause-finally.

quiz.question: What preposition is used to indicate the agent ('by') in a passive sentence?
quiz.explanation: The agent in Afrikaans passive structures is introduced with 'deur'.

quiz.question: Convert active 'Pieter bou die muur' to present passive:
options: Die muur word deur Pieter gebou.
Die muur is deur Pieter gebou.
Die muur sal deur Pieter bou.
Die muur het deur Pieter gebou.
quiz.explanation: 'Word + ge-participle' is the correct formulation for the present passive.

tip: A classic English speaker trap: 'The car is washed' in Afrikaans means it HAS BEEN washed ('is gewas'). If it is happening right now, use 'word gewas'!

title: Infinitive Clauses with 'Om ... Te'
subtitle: Framing purpose and complement clauses cleanly at sentence ends
keyPoint: Infinitive clauses are framed by placing 'om' at the beginning of the clause and the particle 'te' immediately before the main infinitive at the very end.

cells: Ek oefen om fiks te bly
Hy probeer om vroeg te kom
Dit is maklik om te leer
om nie laat te wees nie

useCases.label: Expressing Purpose
useCases.example: Hy gaan winkel toe om kos te koop.

useCases.label: Complements of Desire/Attempt
useCases.example: Ons beplan om volgende week te trek.

useCases.label: Negative Infinitive Clauses
useCases.example: Ek belowe om nie weer te jok nie.

examples.en: Dit is lekker om saam te kuier.
Sy leer hard om die eksamen te slaag.
Hulle het besluit om 'n nuwe motor te koop.
Moenie vergeet om die deur te sluit nie.
Dit is belangrik om elke dag water te drink.
examples.highlight: om elke dag water te drink

mistakes.wrong: Hy hardloop te haal die bus.
mistakes.right: Hy hardloop om die bus te haal.
mistakes.note: Unlike English 'to catch', Afrikaans requires the two-part bracket 'om ... te + verb'.

mistakes.wrong: Dit is moeilik om te verstaan dit.
mistakes.right: Dit is moeilik om dit te verstaan.
mistakes.note: All objects and modifiers must sit between 'om' and 'te'; 'te + verb' must stay at the very end.

mistakes.wrong: Sy het vergeet om te die melk koop.
mistakes.right: Sy het vergeet om die melk te koop.
mistakes.note: 'Te' must directly precede the infinitive verb, not the noun phrase.

quiz.question: Complete the purpose clause: 'Ek werk hard ___ geld ___ verdien.'
quiz.explanation: Infinitive clauses are framed using 'om' at the beginning and 'te' before the verb at the end.

quiz.question: Where does the object 'Afrikaans' go in 'Dit is lekker om (leer) (Afrikaans) (te)'?
quiz.explanation: The object sits inside the frame: 'om' + [object] + 'te' + [verb].

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly expresses 'He tries not to fall'?
options: Hy probeer om te nie val nie.
Hy probeer om val nie te nie.
Hy probeer nie om te val nie.
Hy probeer om nie te val nie.
quiz.explanation: 'Nie' follows 'om', preceding 'te + infinitive', with the second 'nie' closing the clause.

quiz.question: Choose the correctly ordered sentence:
options: Ons beplan om môre na die strand te gaan.
Ons beplan te gaan môre na die strand om.
Ons beplan om te gaan môre na die strand.
Ons beplan na die strand om môre te gaan.
quiz.explanation: 'Om' opens the clause after the main verb, followed by time and place, ending in 'te gaan'.

tip: Treat 'om ... te' like a sandwich: 'om' is the top slice of bread, 'te + verb' is the bottom slice, and all objects and details go in the middle!

title: Relative Clauses with 'Wat' and Compound Relatives
subtitle: Connecting sentences seamlessly with invariant 'wat' and 'waar-' compounds
keyPoint: Afrikaans uses the invariant pronoun 'wat' for both persons and things as subject or object, but switches to 'waar-' compounds when the antecedent is governed by a preposition.

cells: Die man met wie sy praat

useCases.label: Subject Relative
useCases.example: Die meisie wat daar sing, is my suster.

useCases.label: Compound with Waar-
useCases.example: Die pen waarmee ek skryf, is blou.

useCases.label: Person with Preposition
useCases.example: Die vriende aan wie ons dink, bly ver.

examples.en: Die vrou wat langs my woon, is baie vriendelik.
Hier is die huis waarin ons grootgeword het.
Die probleem waaroor almal praat, is ingewikkeld.
Die kinders wat buite speel, maak baie geraas.
Die man na wie sy luister, is 'n professor.

mistakes.wrong: Die man wie daar staan is lank.
mistakes.right: Die man wat daar staan is lank.
mistakes.note: Use 'wat' as the relative subject pronoun for people, never 'wie'.

mistakes.wrong: Die tafel op wat die boek lê.
mistakes.right: Die tafel waarop die boek lê.
mistakes.note: Never use 'prep + wat'; merge into a 'waar-' compound ('waarop') for inanimate antecedents.

mistakes.wrong: Die vrou waarmee hy getroud is.
mistakes.right: Die vrou met wie hy getroud is.
mistakes.note: For human antecedents after a preposition, use '[preposition] + wie', not 'waar-'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Die student ___ die prys gewen het, is baie slim.'
quiz.explanation: The invariant relative pronoun 'wat' is used for both people and things acting as subjects.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The instrument with which he plays'?
options: Die instrument met wat hy speel
Die instrument met wie hy speel
Die instrument wat hy mee speel
quiz.explanation: Inanimate antecedents with prepositions combine into 'waar-' compounds ('waar' + 'met' -> 'waarmee').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence referring to a person: 'Die dokter na ___ sy luister...'
quiz.explanation: When referring to a person after a preposition ('na'), use 'wie' ('na wie').

quiz.question: Identify the incorrect relative phrase:
options: die huis in wat ons woon
quiz.explanation: 'In wat' is incorrect; Afrikaans requires the compound 'waarin'.

tip: Simple rule of thumb: Use 'wat' for regular descriptions (people and things). When a preposition is involved, use '[prep] + wie' for people, and 'waar-[prep]' for things!

title: Complex Negation with Inherent Negative Words
subtitle: Master the sentence-final 'nie' when using negative adverbs and pronouns
keyPoint: When an inherently negative word like 'nooit', 'niemand', or 'nêrens' begins the negation, the first 'nie' is omitted but the clause-final 'nie' is still required.

cells: Ons kan dit nêrens vind nie.
Sy het geen geld oor nie.

useCases.label: Denying frequency with 'nooit'
useCases.example: Ek het nog nooit daardie fliek gesien nie.

useCases.label: Denying persons with 'niemand'
useCases.example: Niemand praat vandag in die klas nie.

useCases.label: Denying location with 'nêrens'
useCases.example: Hulle kan die verlore sleutels nêrens kry nie.

examples.en: Ek het nooit daardie storie geglo nie.
Niemand wil vandag buite in die reën speel nie.
examples.highlight: Niemand wil vandag buite in die reën speel nie

examples.en: Ons het nêrens 'n oop winkel gesien nie.
Daar is geen rede vir kommer nie.
Hy sê niks oor die plan nie.

mistakes.wrong: Niemand het die man gesien.
mistakes.right: Niemand het die man gesien nie.
mistakes.note: Inherently negative words still require the closing sentence-final 'nie'.

mistakes.wrong: Ek het nie nooit gerook nie.
mistakes.note: Do not put a first 'nie' right before or after 'nooit'; the inherent negative word replaces 'nie 1'.

mistakes.wrong: Hy het nie geen geld nie.
mistakes.note: Avoid double-marking 'nie' before 'geen'; use only 'geen' plus the sentence-final 'nie'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Niemand ken die pad na die dorp ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'Niemand' acts as the first negative element, so the sentence must close with the final 'nie'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence for 'I have never seen him.'
options: Ek het nie hom nooit gesien.
Ek het hom nooit gesien nie.
Ek het nie hom gesien nie nooit.
quiz.explanation: 'Nooit' replaces the first 'nie', and the clause must conclude with 'nie'.

quiz.question: Which word correctly completes: 'Ons soek die hond, maar hy is ___ te vinde nie'?
quiz.explanation: 'Nêrens' (nowhere) fits the context of searching without success, followed by final 'nie'.

quiz.question: Identify the grammatically correct negative statement:
options: Daar is nie water in die beker nie geen.
Daar is geen water in die beker.
Daar is nie geen water in die beker nie.
Daar is geen water in die beker nie.
quiz.explanation: 'Geen' takes the place of the first negative marker and requires a final 'nie' at clause end.

tip: Think of Afrikaans negation as a bracket: inherently negative words like 'niks', 'niemand', and 'nooit' open the bracket, but you must still close it with 'nie' at the end!

title: Modal Past Tenses and 'Sou'
subtitle: Use irregular past modals without 'het' or the 'ge-' prefix
keyPoint: Afrikaans expresses past modality and conditional mood directly through 'wou', 'kon', 'moes', and 'sou', keeping the lexical verb in bare infinitive form without 'ge-'.

cells: Hy kon die swaar tas dra.

useCases.label: Past necessity with 'moes'
useCases.example: Hulle moes die eksamen gister skryf.

useCases.label: Past ability with 'kon'
useCases.example: Ek kon die probleem maklik oplos.

useCases.label: Hypothetical condition with 'sou'
useCases.example: As ek ryk was, sou ek reis.

examples.en: Ek wou gister vir jou bel.
Die kinders kon nie die boom klim nie.
examples.highlight: kon nie die boom klim nie

examples.en: Ons moes die motor dadelik stop.
Sy sou die kos maak as sy tyd gehad het.
Niemand kon die antwoord uitwerk nie.

mistakes.wrong: Ek het gewou huis toe gaan.
mistakes.note: Do not use 'het gewou'. 'Wou' alone serves as the past tense.

mistakes.wrong: Ons moes die deur gesluit.
mistakes.note: The main verb with a modal past does not take the past prefix 'ge-'.

mistakes.wrong: Hy het gekon swem toe hy jonk was.
mistakes.right: Hy kon swem toe hy jonk was.
mistakes.note: Use 'kon' directly instead of constructing an auxiliary compound like 'het gekon'.

quiz.question: Complete the past modal: 'Hulle ___ gister die rekening betaal.' (had to)
quiz.explanation: 'Moes' is the simple past form of 'moet' (had to / should have).

quiz.question: Choose the correct translation: 'I wanted to sleep early.'
quiz.explanation: 'Wou' is used on its own with the bare infinitive 'slaap' (without 'ge-').

quiz.question: Complete the conditional clause: 'As hy hard studeer het, ___ hy geslaag het.' (would)
quiz.explanation: 'Sou' denotes the hypothetical conditional 'would' in counterfactual and conditional statements.

quiz.question: Select the sentence with correct verb morphology:
options: Sy het gekon die hek oopmaak.
Sy het die hek kan oopmaak.
quiz.explanation: 'Kon' is paired directly with the bare infinitive 'oopmaak' without 'het' or 'ge-'.

tip: Even though standard Afrikaans lost most simple past tenses, modals are the shining exception: memorize 'wou', 'kon', 'moes', and 'sou' as standalone past verbs without ever adding 'ge-'!

title: Reduplication of Verbs and Adverbs
subtitle: Express manner, duration, and intensity with twin words
keyPoint: Reduplicating verbs and adverbs with a hyphen creates adverbials indicating continuous simultaneous action, gradual development, or heightened intensity.

useCases.label: Simultaneous motion manner
useCases.example: Hy het speel-speel die berg geklim.

useCases.label: Iterative or cautious action
useCases.example: Die meisie het soek-soek deur die kamer gestap.

useCases.label: High frequency repetition
useCases.example: Sy kyk kort-kort op haar horlosie.

examples.en: Die oupa stap praat-praat langs die see.
Hulle het lag-lag die moeilike taak voltooi.
Ons sal nou-nou by die restaurant aankom.
Die seuntjie het val-val oor die rotse gehardloop.
Sy het kyk-kyk in die donker gang afgeloop.

mistakes.wrong: Hy het geloop-geloop na die skool.
mistakes.right: Hy het loop-loop na die skool gestap.
mistakes.note: Do not affix 'ge-' to reduplicated verbal adverbs; keep both stems in bare root form.

mistakes.wrong: Sy het gesing en gesing sonder ophou.
mistakes.right: Sy het sing-sing die werk gedoen.
mistakes.note: While 'gesing en gesing' is emphatic repetition, native idiomatic manner adverbials use the hyphenated reduplication 'sing-sing'.

mistakes.wrong: Ons kom nou nou.
mistakes.note: Reduplicated expressions must be hyphenated in standard Afrikaans orthography.

quiz.question: Which reduplicated form means 'effortlessly / playfully' in: 'Hy het die toets ___ geslaag'?
quiz.explanation: 'Lag-lag' literally means 'laughing-laughing' and idiomatically signifies doing something effortlessly or with ease.

quiz.question: Complete the temporal sentence: 'Die bus vertrek ___.' (very soon / in a minute)
quiz.explanation: 'Nou-nou' means 'in a short moment' or 'very soon'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct spelling for 'repeatedly checking':
quiz.explanation: Verbal reduplication uses the bare verb root joined by a hyphen without any past participle 'ge-'.

quiz.question: In 'Sy het soek-soek haar pad gevind', what does 'soek-soek' express?
options: Manner of proceeding cautiously while searching
quiz.explanation: Reduplicating 'soek' functions adverbially to describe acting while searching along the way.

tip: Reduplication is one of Afrikaans's unique Khoisan and Malay-influenced syntactic charms; pair identical base verb roots with a hyphen to turn actions into expressive adverbs of manner!

title: Indirect Commands and Subjunctive Equivalents
subtitle: Report desires, requests, and commands with 'moet', 'laat', and bare infinitives
keyPoint: Because Afrikaans has no morphological subjunctive, indirect commands and reported wishes use 'dat ... moet', causative 'laat', or a bare infinitive clause.

cells: ... dat die man dadelik moet kom.
Hy vra om die brief te lees.

useCases.label: Indirect orders with 'dat ... moet'
useCases.example: Die dokter beveel aan dat hy meer moet rus.

useCases.label: Permissive or imperative 'laat'
useCases.example: Laat die kinders dadelik binnekom.

useCases.label: Desire for another agent to act
useCases.example: Ek wil hê dat jy die waarheid moet praat.

examples.en: Die polisie beveel dat almal moet staan.
My ma vra dat ons die tafel moet dek.
examples.highlight: dat ons die tafel moet dek

examples.en: Laat hy dadelik sy werk klaarmaak.
examples.highlight: Laat hy dadelik sy werk klaarmaak

examples.en: Ek stel voor dat ons liewer môre moet ry.
examples.highlight: dat ons liewer môre moet ry

examples.en: Sy wil hê dat haar broer moet luister.

mistakes.wrong: Die baas wil hê dat ek doen die werk.
mistakes.right: Die baas wil hê dat ek die werk moet doen.
mistakes.note: Subordinate 'dat' clauses require secondary verbs and modals at the end, and commands require 'moet'.

mistakes.wrong: Hy beveel my om te moet vertrek.
mistakes.right: Hy beveel my om te vertrek.
mistakes.note: Do not combine 'om te' with 'moet'; use either 'om ... te + verb' or 'dat ... moet'.

mistakes.wrong: Ek wil dat jy kom.
mistakes.right: Ek wil hê dat jy moet kom.
mistakes.note: In Afrikaans, 'wil' cannot take a 'dat'-clause directly; you must say 'wil hê dat...'.

quiz.question: Complete the indirect command: 'Die kaptein beveel dat die bemanning gereed ___.'
quiz.explanation: Indirect orders introduced by 'dat' rely on the modal auxiliary 'moet' placed clause-finally.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly renders: 'I want you to tell the truth'?
options: Ek wil dat jy die waarheid sê.
Ek wil hê jy die waarheid te praat.
Ek wil hê dat jy die waarheid moet praat.
Ek wil hê vir jou om praat die waarheid.
quiz.explanation: Afrikaans requires 'wil hê dat...' followed by the subject and 'moet' for wanting someone else to perform an act.

quiz.question: Select the correct causative construction for 'Let him go':
quiz.explanation: 'Laat' takes an object pronoun and a bare infinitive without 'te': 'Laat hom gaan'.

quiz.question: Correct the error: 'Die onderwyser vra dat die klas stil wees.'
options: Die onderwyser vra dat die klas moet stil wees.
Die onderwyser vra om die klas stil wees.
Die onderwyser vra dat moet die klas stil wees.
Die onderwyser vra die klas om stil wees.
quiz.explanation: The subordinate clause with 'dat' requires the modal 'moet' placed at the end: '...moet stil wees'.

tip: Never translate 'I want you to [do something]' as 'Ek wil dat jy...'. Always remember the formula: 'Ek wil hê dat [onderwerp] moet [werkwoord]'!

title: Continuous Aspect through Hendiadys (V1 en V2)
subtitle: Form progressive aspect with paired posture verbs 'sit en', 'staan en', 'lê en', and 'loop en'
keyPoint: Afrikaans expresses ongoing progressive aspect by joining a posture verb ('sit', 'staan', 'lê', 'loop') with 'en' and a bare second verb without any infinitive markers.

cells: is sitting reading / in the middle of reading
is pacing thinking / wandering about thinking

useCases.label: Sedentary ongoing activity
useCases.example: Ouma sit en brei 'n warm trui.

useCases.label: Upright progressive action
useCases.example: Hulle staan en wag al vir 'n uur vir die bus.

useCases.label: Past progressive with 'het'
useCases.example: Hy het die hele middag gelê en slaap.

examples.en: Pa sit en kyk na die nuus op televisie.
Die kinders staan en kyk na die voëls.
Die hond lê en droom in die son.
Hy loop en wonder oor sy toekoms.
Ons het ure lank gesit en gesels.

mistakes.wrong: Hy sit om te lees 'n koerant.
mistakes.note: Afrikaans does not use 'om te' for continuous posture hendiadys; connect with 'en' directly.

mistakes.wrong: Ons het gesit en lees die boek.
mistakes.right: Ons het gesit en die boek gelees.
mistakes.note: In compound past tenses, the second verb moves to the end of the clause and receives 'ge-' (or both verbs take 'ge-').

mistakes.wrong: Sy is besig om te sit en sing.
mistakes.note: Avoid clumsy stacking of 'besig om te' with posture verbs; 'sit en sing' already conveys progressive aspect.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'He is lying down listening to music':
options: Hy lê te luister na musiek.
Hy lê en luister na musiek.
Hy lê om na musiek te luister.
Hy is luister en lê na musiek.
quiz.explanation: The continuous hendiadys pairs 'lê' + 'en' + bare verb 'luister'.

quiz.question: How do you form the past tense of 'Hy sit en werk'?
quiz.explanation: In standard past tense hendiadys, both verbal elements generally take the prefix: 'het gesit en gewerk'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Die studente ___ en gesels voor die biblioteek.' (are standing)
quiz.explanation: 'Staan en' indicates an ongoing, standing progressive activity.

quiz.question: What nuance does 'loop en' convey in 'Hy loop en kla oor die werk'?
options: An ongoing action carried out while moving about
quiz.explanation: 'Loop en [verb]' expresses that an action is taking place continuously or repeatedly while walking/moving around.

tip: Instead of relying on the English '-ing' form or the cumbersome 'besig om te', native Afrikaans speakers almost always use 'sit en', 'staan en', 'lê en', or 'loop en' to describe what someone is doing right now!
